dict.string:
Anime Multi Source Agent (AMSA) by Dingmatt (GitHub) combines the sources below.
Evolved from the HTTP AniDB Metadata Agent (HAMA):
HAMA was created by Atomicstrawberry and is maintained by ZeroQI. Always sharing good ideas.
Show and episode information, titles, tags, cast, ratings and posters from AniDB:
AniDB.net is a non-profit, community-run database of anime information, freely open to the public.
Episodes, season texts, artwork, content ratings and writers/directors from TheTVDB:
Metadata provided by TheTVDB. Please consider adding missing information or subscribing.
AniDB to TVDB episode mapping and movie-set collections from the Anime-Lists project:
Anime-Lists (anime-list-master.xml and anime-movieset-list.xml), started by ScudLee and maintained by the Anime-Lists contributors.
Titles, summaries, ratings, cast (including English voice actors), posters and banners from AniList:
AniList, via its public GraphQL API. AniList ids are also looked up with the ARM id mapping service.
Cross-site ids, airing status and extra titles from the anime-offline-database:
cedya77/anime-offline-database, continuing manami-project/anime-offline-database, made available under the Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0, with contents under the Database Contents License (DbCL) v1.0.
Missing episode titles, summaries and air dates from MyAnimeList and Kitsu:
MyAnimeList data through Jikan, the unofficial MyAnimeList API; and Kitsu.
Opening and ending song titles and artists from AnimeThemes:
AnimeThemes, a community archive of anime opening and ending themes.
Theme music from Plex:
Plex's TV theme music service (tvthemes.plexapp.com).
Includes this library:
Unidecode by Tomaž Šolc (GNU GPL v2 or later), for transliterating titles.
